title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 56
paragraphs: What language the Pelasgians used to speak I am not able to say with certainty. But if one must pronounce judging by those Pelasgians who still remain—those who dwelt in the city of Creston above the Tyrsenians, and who were once neighbors of the race now called Dorian, dwelling then in the land now called Thessaliotis, and also by those Pelasgians who remain from the settlers at Placia and Scylace in the region of the Hellespont, who before that had been fellow-settlers with the Athenians, and by the natives of the various other towns which are really Pelasgian, though they have lost the name—if one must judge by these, then the Pelasgians used to speak a barbarian language. If, therefore, the whole Pelasgian race was like these, then the Attic race, being Pelasgian, must at the same time that it changed and became Hellenic have unlearned its language as well. For the people of Creston do not speak the same language as any of those who dwell around them, nor do the people of Placia; but they speak the same language as one another. And by this it is proved that they still preserve unchanged the form of speech which they brought with them when they migrated to these places.
